title: StarterPack
summary: The tool template container: Tools parented here are copied into each player's Backpack on spawn. Runtime inventory changes happen on the Backpack, not here.

details.heading: Lifecycle
details.body: At spawn, Tools in StarterPack are cloned into the player's Backpack (under the Player). Equipping moves a Tool from Backpack to Character; unequipping returns it.

explanation.whatItIs: The default loadout: every tool you put here shows up in every player's backpack when they spawn.
explanation.whyItExists: Games need starting equipment without scripting it per player.
whenToUse: Starting tools every player should have
Template tools you'll also clone dynamically for rewards
whenNotToUse: For giving tools mid-game — clone into player.Backpack directly
For tools that shouldn't reset on death — manage manually and set respawn behavior
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
StarterPack (template)          Player
 ├─ Sword            ─spawn→   Backpack
 └─ Potion           ─spawn→    ├─ Sword
                                 └─ Potion
Equipping: Backpack → Character (Tool welds to hand via Handle)
```
tips: A Tool needs a part named `Handle` to be holdable (unless RequiresHandle = false)
Tool.Activated fires on click/tap while equipped — the main interaction hook
commonMistakes: Parenting runtime-given tools to StarterPack instead of the player's Backpack
Missing Handle part → tool equips but floats/doesn't render correctly

examples.title: Giving a tool mid-game
examples.code:
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local function rewardTool(player, toolName)
    local template = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(toolName)
    if not template then return end
    local tool = template:Clone()
    tool.Parent = player:WaitForChild("Backpack")   -- appears in inventory
end
